headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors from shared filesystem/git; both agents can write and execute shell by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP, while Plandex reads/writes the project directory and stages changes before apply. Because both can touch shared filesystem/git state, attacker-controlled content from one can be consumed by the other as instructions. The bridge is not a direct chat channel, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF one agent writes prompt-like text into files the other later reads
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable MCP on Gemini CLI for shared repos
Require manual review of any file containing instructions before reuse
Use read-only mounts for one agent during the other's run

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and files in the working directory, and both have broad network egress. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, either agent can ingest them and send them to its backend or model provider. This is a default workspace exposure rather than a proven exfiltration path, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared project directory
IF either agent is configured to process those files without redaction
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use per-agent cloned repos with different sensitive-file filters
Add a pre-run secret scan and redact matches
Block outbound network for the agent handling sensitive files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell, write files, and modify git state. Gemini CLI shares state via filesystem and git; Plandex shares state via its backend and stages changes before apply. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and no locking is documented here. This is a default dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository
IF they run concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Serialize access with a simple file lock
Assign each agent a separate branch
Disable auto-apply while the other agent is active
Run one agent in a disposable clone

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is explicitly a planner with review-then-apply, but Gemini CLI can emit tool-driven outputs and file edits that Plandex may treat as inputs. If Plandex accepts Gemini-produced artifacts without verification, a mistaken or malicious suggestion can cascade into staged or applied changes. The pair lacks a documented cross-agent verification boundary, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Plandex ingests Gemini-generated files or diffs as authoritative
IF review-then-apply is bypassed or auto-apply is enabled
mitigations: Require human review of Gemini-produced diffs before Plandex applies them
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex
Use a checksum or signed handoff file between agents
Limit Gemini to drafting only, not editing shared files

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no stated regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance issue visible is that both can handle files and send data to external APIs, which creates policy risk if regulated data is placed in the workspace. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so low is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is stored in the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to external model APIs
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use a local-only model backend where permitted
Add a data-classification gate before runs
Document retention and deletion expectations for both tools
